seoTitle: Mary Magdalene Storybook for Children | Called by Name
seoDescription: Mary Magdalene storybook for ages 6-12: nine illustrated narrative pages from Galilee to the Easter garden, with flowing narration and a family reflection.
intro: Walk with Mary from the roads of Galilee to the Easter garden. Read together, then listen for the people beside you.
shortAnswer: This nine-page Mary Magdalene storybook for ages 6 to 12 follows Mary as she travels with Jesus, stays near the cross with other women and becomes a witness to the resurrection, following John's Gospel for the Easter encounter. It ends with a narrated family reflection to share together.
summaryHtml:
Mary Magdalene travels with Jesus, stays near the cross with other women, and becomes a witness to his resurrection. The Easter encounter follows John's Gospel. Nine narrative pages end with a narrated family reflection.

What This Story Covers

  • Mary of Magdala
  • On the roads with Jesus
  • Beside the cross
  • The stone was moved
  • Mary stayed
  • Called by name
  • A message for the others
  • Remembered by the Church
  • Her witness remains
familyReadingHtml:
With a parent or caregiver, read John 20:11-18. Listen for the moment when Mary recognizes Jesus and the message he gives her.

The final page offers a question, Bible reading, a listening action and an original prayer. A trusted adult can help children with the sad parts of the story. Prayer does not replace rest, care or treatment.
aboutHtml:
Illustrations are imaginative composites, not eyewitness reconstructions. This story uses Luke for Mary's earlier discipleship and John for the Easter encounter; the large stone is a detail from Matthew. It does not identify Mary Magdalene with Mary of Bethany or the unnamed woman who anointed Jesus. Page eight shows later Christian remembrance, not Mary alive in a later century. The final reflection is original, not historical dialogue.

Sources: USCCB: Luke 8, women accompanying Jesus; USCCB: John 19, the cross and burial; USCCB: John 20, the Easter encounter; USCCB: Matthew 27, the tomb stone; Holy See: Mary Magdalene, apostle of the apostles (2016); Vatican News: July 22 feast;

faq.a: A disciple of Jesus who supported his ministry and witnessed his resurrection. This retelling follows Luke's account of her discipleship and John's account of the Easter encounter.
Children ages 6 to 12, reading or listening with family. Nine illustrated narrative pages lead to a four-part family reflection.

faq.q: Why is she called the apostle of the apostles?
faq.a: The title honors the resurrection message Mary brought to the disciples. It does not mean that she was one of the Twelve. The Church celebrates her feast on July 22.
